findings.title: Flagged TableWidgetVisualization branch renders a hard-coded empty table
findings.body: When the organization has the `use-table-widget-visualization` feature, the table branch renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}} />` instead of passing the actual `result`/`fields`/`result.meta`. Any org with the flag enabled will see completely blank table widgets (no headers, no rows) rather than their data. The real query results must be mapped into `TabularData`/`TabularColumn` before this can be enabled.

findings.title: Error/breadcrumb timestamps compared in different units
findings.body: In `gen_request_data`, error timestamps come from nodestore event data (`data.get("timestamp")`, seconds since epoch) while rrweb replay events use millisecond epoch timestamps. The merge loop compares `error_events[error_idx]["timestamp"] < event.get("timestamp", 0)` directly, so every error will always compare as earlier than every replay event and all error log lines will be emitted before any breadcrumb, destroying the chronological interleaving the function is meant to produce. One side needs unit normalization.

findings.title: fetch_error_details pairs error ids with node values by position
findings.body: `zip(error_ids, events.values())` assumes `nodestore.backend.get_multi` returns a dict whose value ordering matches the order of `error_ids`. That is an implementation detail of the backend (and of how it builds its result dict); if the ordering differs, each `ErrorEvent.id` will be attached to a different event's title/message/timestamp, producing silently wrong summaries. Index by node id instead: build `node_id -> error_id` and look up `events[node_id]`.

findings.title: get_environment_info fetches a recommended event per issue
findings.body: `get_environment_info` calls `issue.get_recommended_event()` and then `get_environment()` for each of the up-to-5 issues while building a PR comment. Each call is an additional snuba/nodestore + DB round trip inside a task that previously only used fields already loaded on the Group. This noticeably increases latency/cost for every merged-PR comment; consider batching or caching the environment lookup.

findings.title: One invalid report rejects an entire browser report batch
findings.body: Browsers send batches of reports to the Reporting API endpoint. The new loop returns 422 as soon as any single report fails validation, discarding the valid reports in the same request. Since the browser will retry the whole batch, one malformed/unknown report type permanently blocks collection of the others. Prefer validating per report and skipping (with a metric/log) the invalid ones while returning 200.

findings.title: age/timestamp mutual-exclusion checks use truthiness
findings.body: `validate_timestamp` checks `self.initial_data.get("age")` and `validate_age` checks `self.initial_data.get("timestamp")` for truthiness. A report with `age: 0` (very common — a report generated just now) plus a `timestamp` will not be flagged, and `timestamp: 0` likewise. Use `is not None` / `in self.initial_data`. Also, neither field is required, so a report with neither `age` nor `timestamp` passes validation entirely.

findings.title: Analytics recorded before feature gate and schema validation
findings.body: `analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...)` runs before the `features.has(...)` check and before request validation, so the event is emitted even for orgs without the feature (404 responses) and for malformed requests. This inflates the metric and makes it unusable for measuring real assembles. Move the call after the feature check.

findings.title: useTraceItemAttributeKeys can now return undefined attributes
findings.body: Previously `attributes` was always a `TagCollection` (built with `useMemo` from `result.data ?? []`). It is now `isFetching ? previous : data`, where both `previous` and `data` can be `undefined` (first load, or when `enabled` is false / query errors). Callers doing `Object.keys(attributes)` or spreading it will throw at runtime. Default to `{}` or update the return type and all consumers.

findings.title: dcg_to_slow_conditions now keyed only by dcg_ids, risking KeyError
findings.body: `get_condition_query_groups` previously computed slow conditions from `event_data.dcg_to_groups.keys()`, and `get_groups_to_fire` from `event_data.dcg_ids`. Both now receive a single map built from `event_data.dcg_ids`, and both still index it with `dcg_to_slow_conditions[dcg.id]`. If `dcg_to_groups` contains any group id not present in `dcg_ids` (or `get_slow_conditions_for_groups` omits ids with no slow conditions rather than returning a defaultdict), this raises KeyError and the whole delayed-workflow batch fails. Use `.get(dcg.id, [])` or assert the key sets are identical.

findings.title: Comment points at a migration that does not exist in this change
findings.body: Both 0917 and 0920 now say "See 0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py for the correct migration", but no 0921 migration is added in this PR. Readers (and anyone auditing why the data migration was neutered) will look for a file that isn't there; either land the replacement migration in the same change or reword the comment.

findings.title: enabled guard `Boolean(normalizedDateRange)` is always true
findings.body: `normalizeDateTimeParams` returns an object, so `Boolean(normalizedDateRange)` is unconditionally `true` and contributes nothing to the `enabled` condition. If the intent was to wait until page filters are ready, check `usePageFilters().isReady` or a specific field instead; as written the query may fire with default/unready filters.
